arms.better: tm found the faulty append and produced the right surgical fix, and it recovered after its first temporary repro failed because the requested working directory was outside the project root. It repeatedly reread completions.go and overlapping command.go ranges, however, consuming 2,378,178 tokens by tm stats and 632 seconds for this small change; the captured usage events total only 153,045 tokens, so the stats number also needs reconciliation. The progress transcript is a dense stream of repeated read/search actions. The final message says the ticket was submitted, while the CLI separately says it must be reviewed and accepted or rejected; users could mistake submission for completion or be unsure what action remains. A tighter scoped plan, reuse of prior file context, trustworthy usage totals, and a clear final status with the next command would improve the experience.

OpenCode quickly narrowed the issue to getCompletions, implemented a copy-before-append fix, added a focused regression test, and ran go test ./... successfully. Its initial semantic search failed because no local index existed and its filename glob missed completions.go, but it switched to an exact search and recovered without getting stuck. It could make the plan and fallback from the unavailable index more explicit to the user, and its JSON reported cost as zero despite a substantial token total; clearer usage/cost availability would make the run easier to assess.
